# Brief 485: read-only closed fiscal years (E-06, #230 item 4). Do NOT commit; no package.json / migrations / app.module. Do not edit modules/posting_rules, modules/treasury, modules/cheques.

Work in your cwd (git worktree), code in output_apps/enterprise_hub/modules/accounting.

## What I found (verify, do not trust blindly)
- Closing a fiscal year (`services/fiscal-year.service.ts` close) creates a period lock (`createPeriodLock`, row id stored as `fiscal_year.periodLockId`) and sets the year CLOSED. Reopen calls `accountingRepository.unlockPeriod` directly.
- Enforcement is central: `repositories/accounting.repository.ts` `persistJournalEntry` (throws `LockedPeriodError`, pg trigger RX003 backs it), `assertDateOpen` (used by `updateVoucher`, `changeVoucherStatus` to POSTED). `AccountingService.postEntry` maps it to `PeriodLockedException` (423) with an ENGLISH message "Posting refused: ... locked accounting period" in two places (postEntry catch and `mapPeriodLock`).
- Other modules (invoicing, inventory, payroll, fixed assets, petty cash, cheques, treasury, banking, invoice_capture, data_import) post through `createJournalEntry`/`postTypedEntry` (via posting_rules or directly).
Suspected leaks to confirm by test first, then fix centrally:
 1. `AccountingService.unlockPeriod` can unlock the lock that belongs to a CLOSED fiscal year (via POST period-locks/:id/unlock), leaving the year CLOSED but the ledger writable. Fix: in `unlockPeriod`, refuse (ConflictException or PeriodLockedException, Persian message, e.g. "این قفل مربوط به سال مالی بسته‌شده است؛ ابتدا سال مالی را بازگشایی کنید.") when a fiscal year with status CLOSED references this lock id. Inject the FiscalYearRepository only if it is already available in AccountingService; otherwise add a small repository method on AccountingRepository that checks `fin_fiscal_years.period_lock_id = :id AND status='CLOSED'`. Reopen (fiscal-year.service) must keep working (it uses the repository directly).
 2. `deleteVoucher` of a DRAFT/TEMPORARY voucher dated inside a locked period is allowed. Fix: `assertDateOpen` on the voucher date first (refuse with the same Persian 423).
 3. `updateVoucher` only checks the NEW date; editing a voucher whose CURRENT date is locked and moving it out must also be refused (check both old and new date).
 4. Make the two English "Posting refused" strings one helper with a Persian message including the date, e.g. `ثبت سند در دورهٔ قفل‌شده مجاز نیست: تاریخ ${date} در دوره یا سال مالی بسته قرار دارد.` (check no spec asserts the old English text: grep first; update those that do.)
 5. Reversal rule: read `reverseWithin` + `postEntry`: a reversal dated in an OPEN period of a voucher that sits in a CLOSED period is allowed (new entry dated by options.date, default today); a reversal dated inside the closed period is refused 423. Do not change that, test it, and also confirm that reversing a closing entry through the normal reverse endpoint stays refused (existing 400).
 Report anything else you find (e.g. a path that writes fin_journal_entries/lines without going through persistJournalEntry/assertDateOpen).

## Tests to write (new): `modules/accounting/closed-fiscal-year.pg.spec.ts`
Copy the DB bootstrap from `voucher-states.pg.spec.ts` (opt-in on ROXIRA_TEST_PG_HOST, throwaway DB). Build the services as `fiscal-close.pg.spec.ts` does (read it for FiscalYearService wiring and how a year is created+closed). Create a Jalali-style fiscal year (use the dates fiscal-close.pg.spec.ts uses), post a voucher inside it, CLOSE the year, then expect each refusal with HTTP 423 (or 409 for the unlock case) AND the Persian message (assert with a Persian substring, e.g. toThrow(/قفل|بسته/)):
 - createJournalEntry dated in the year; postTypedEntry dated in the year
 - createJournalEntry as DRAFT/TEMPORARY dated in the year is allowed or refused? Read persistJournalEntry; assert whatever the code does and state it in the final report (drafts do not touch balances).
 - updateVoucher (draft created before close, dated inside) -> refused; changeVoucherStatus to POSTED -> refused; deleteVoucher -> refused (after your fix)
 - reverseJournalEntry of the in-year voucher with date inside the year -> 423; with date in the next open year -> succeeds and balances net to zero
 - unlockPeriod on the year's lock -> refused; after FiscalYearService.reopen -> everything writable again
 - petty cash (PettyCashService, see petty-cash.pg.spec.ts for wiring), fixed-asset depreciation posting (FixedAssetService, fixed-assets.pg.spec.ts) dated in the closed year -> refused with 423. If wiring is more than ~40 lines, skip that one and say so.
 Plus a pure/static guard spec `modules/accounting/ledger-write-paths.spec.ts`: scan all non-spec .ts files under modules/ with fs: `persistJournalEntry(` is called only in accounting.service.ts (+ definition in repository); no other file contains `INSERT INTO fin_journal_entries` / `.into(JournalEntryEntity)` outside accounting.repository.ts. List allowed files explicitly so a new leak fails the test.
Run: `cd output_apps/enterprise_hub && /home/mahan/Developer/roxira-wt/_fleet/heavy.sh env ROXIRA_TEST_PG_HOST=127.0.0.1 ROXIRA_TEST_PG_PORT=55433 ROXIRA_TEST_PG_USER=postgres npx jest --runInBand modules/accounting/closed-fiscal-year.pg.spec.ts` and the static spec; also rerun existing accounting.ledger.pg.spec.ts, voucher-states.pg.spec.ts, fiscal-close.pg.spec.ts, accounting.ledger-integrity.spec.ts to be sure nothing regressed. Final output: a table path -> where enforced -> test name, and the list of leaks found/fixed.
